h: פָּרָשַׁת שְׁקָלִים, מַאֲמָר ח׳ Parshas Shekalim — Maamar Ches

p: In the Zohar Chadash (beginning of Parshas Ki Sisa):
What is "everyone who passes among those counted"
if he wishes to be rectified
to bring it close to "zos," etc.,
what is explicit and pointed to with the finger,
as it will be in the future,
when each one will point with his finger
and so too at the Splitting of the Sea,
וְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב סד, ב)
a maidservant saw at the Sea
they merited to say, "This is my G-d."
And "zos" alludes to the attribute of Malchus,
as they said in the holy Zohar
one also merits that it be explicit,
as though pointing with the finger — "zos" —
only that it is in the feminine form.
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ג רל, א)
He is truth and She is faith —
that Hashem Yisbarach stands over him
that it be as though explicit before his eyes.
And then too they recognize the unity,
just as in your heart there is only One,
so in our heart there is none but He;
even though we do not recognize the unity
we recognize that there is only One,
as has been explained many times
as they said in the holy Zohar
the heh was a dalet, etc.
That is, there shine in the attribute of Malchus
and the aleph, which indicates the supernal Pele:
And through the corruption of the Calf
so that there was no unity
of Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah.
the kaf alludes to Keser Elyon,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רנו, ב)
"Anochi" — in it the kaf is Keser.
And the half shekel, ten gerah,
is the secret of the yud,
as they said in the Zohar Chadash (ibid.);
that is, the yud is Chochmah,
And this is what they said: to draw down and to illuminate
in the place that is blemished;
that is, "in the light of the King's face is life";
and this is "the ransom of his soul" —
And it states in the Zohar Chadash (ibid.):
then it is called "the holy shekel,"
the right hand of the King, etc.;
that is, the supernal Kodesh, Chochmah,
as they said in the holy Zohar
That is, it explains that the shekalim
came to atone for the sin of the Calf,
in which they transgressed the commandments of their Master
as they said in the Yerushalmi
(שְׁקָלִים פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ג ט, ב)
and the Tanchuma on Ki Sisa (siman 10).
וְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ח, א)
And it states in the Midrash Rabbah (Vayikra Rabbah 8:1)
and in the Midrash Tanchuma (Ki Sisa 5):
זֶה יַשְׁפִּיל וְזֶה יָרִים [תְּהִלִּים עה, ח]
"This one He lowers and this one He raises" (Tehillim 75:8) —
with the word "zeh" they were lowered:
and with the word "zeh" they were raised:
And in the Pesikta (parshah 10, siman 15) it brings:
"this" lowered Yisrael to the pit of destruction —
(which is what is said in Nechemiah 9:18) —
they merit that there be the unity —
and that they merit it to be explicit to the eye,
to point and say, "This is my G-d"
Afterward it states in the Zohar Chadash:
to atone for the ten tribes
and transgressed the commandment of their Master, etc.
אָמַר לֵיהּ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moshe:
if you wish to raise their heads —
It appears that the Zohar Chadash
זֶה יִתְּנוּ כָּל הָעוֹבֵר עַל הַפְּקוּדִים וְגוֹמֵר
"This they shall give, everyone who passes among those counted," etc.
from the age of," etc., "shall give," etc.
He expounded one on the corruption of the Calf,
and transgressed the commandments of their Master,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ דָּרַשׁ עַל מְכִירַת יוֹסֵף.
and afterward he expounded on the sale of Yosef.
And it concludes: then they are called "the holy shekel,"
because He is half a body
and Knesses Yisrael is half a body, etc.
the lower Chochmah, the lower Kodesh
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קעו, ב)
And this is what they said: "they are called the holy shekel."
That is, Yosef draws down to the attribute of Malchus —
"And when it is blessed from Yesod,
then we call it Kodesh," etc. —
that is, the lower Kodesh, as mentioned above.
and this is the primordial light
דְּזָרַע קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בְּגַן עֵדֶן
which the Holy One, blessed be He, sowed in Gan Eden
who is the gardener of the garden
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קסו, ב)
and on Shabbos — for all agree
that on Shabbos the Torah was given to Yisrael
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א מז, ב)
Torah she'b'al peh we call it."
Parshas Shekalim is read on Shabbos,
for then is the time to merit
"the light of the King's face is life,"

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, beginning of Ki Sisa — “What does ‘everyone who passes over the counted ones’ mean? This is one who transgresses his Master’s commandments. If he wishes to be repaired before his Master, so that the judgment above will not rule over him: ‘This they shall give.’ He must give zeh, bringing it near to zot and illuminating it with radiance, so that the world will not burn in its flames. For one who transgresses his Master’s commandments separates zeh from zot. He must therefore repair that place and lift his head before judgment, so that judgment will not rule over him.” The exposition hears “passes over” as “transgresses” and treats the masculine zeh and feminine zot as the two sides of a union damaged by sin. Rav Tzadok now explains the spiritual meaning of each.

paragraphs.text: Taanis 31a, on Yeshayahu 25:9 — “Ulla of Bira said in Rabbi Elazar’s name: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle for the righteous, and He will sit among them in the Garden of Eden. Each one will point with his finger, as it says: ‘It will be said on that day: Behold, this is our God; we hoped for Him and He saved us. This is Hashem, for whom we hoped; let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.’”

paragraphs.text: Mekhilta, Beshalach, Shirah 3; Zohar II, 64b — “Rabbi Eliezer says: From where do you say that a maidservant saw at the sea what Yeshayahu and Yechezkel did not see? It says: ‘Through the prophets I convey likenesses,’ and: ‘The heavens opened and I saw visions of God.’ A human king enters a city surrounded by guards, mighty men to his right and left and soldiers before and behind; people ask which one is the king. But when the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared at the sea, none needed to ask who He was. Once they saw Him, they recognized Him, and all opened their mouths and said: ‘This is my God, and I will glorify Him.’” Zohar II, 64b likewise invokes the maidservant’s vision when asking how Israel, after seeing the Divine Presence at the sea, could ask whether Hashem was in their midst. The Mekhilta’s point is immediate recognition, the aspect of zeh developed here.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 37b — “Thus we have learned: This crown that is called zot is called ‘woman,’ as it says, ‘This one shall be called woman.’ Why? ‘For from man was this one taken.’ Who is the man? The one called zeh. This is the male man, as it says, ‘For this Moshe, the man.’ He is called ‘this man,’ and zot is taken from zeh, who is called male.” This is the source for the paired demonstratives. The identification of zot with Malchus is part of the passage’s symbolic account of the feminine crown.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Acharei Mos 1 — “Such revelation will be only in the future… but through emunah one can attain this light so that it is explicit, and it is called zos… therefore Shabbos is called zos, for then there is complete faith.” Rav Tzadok there draws the corollary for this maamar’s close: the explicit “zos” of faith belongs above all to Shabbos, the day on which Parshas Shekalim is read.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 230a — “The masters of the Mishnah established: Study is not the principal thing, but action. For the Holy One, blessed be He, is concealed in the mysteries of Torah. Through what is He made known? Through the commandments, which are His Shechinah, His image. Just as He is humble, His Shechinah is humility; He is chasid, and she is chasidah; He is mighty, and she rules over all the nations of the world. He is truth, and she is faith; He is king, and she is kingship; He is wise, and she is His wisdom; He is crown, and she is His diadem.” The paired attributes belong to an explanation of inward divinity becoming manifest through the Shechinah and mitzvos. Rav Tzadok develops the particular pair “truth” and “faith.”

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 56a — “Yaakov sought to reveal the end of days to his sons, but the Shechinah departed from him. He said: Perhaps, Heaven forbid, there is a disqualification among my children, as Avraham had Yishmael and my father Yitzchak had Esav. His sons said to him: ‘Hear, Israel, Hashem is our God, Hashem is One.’ They said: Just as there is only One in your heart, so there is only One in our hearts. At that moment Yaakov our father began and said: ‘Blessed is the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever.’” The words are addressed to their father Israel. The sons affirm the same exclusive allegiance to the One whom Yaakov knows; Rav Tzadok explains their unity of faith without assuming an identical degree of revelation.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 22 — “The letter dalet indicates the complete revelation of Malchus Shamayim, for the hei was a dalet: through lowliness and poverty (dalus) one attains the final hei, the culmination of the revelation of Malchus.” This adds why the dalet of echad marks Knesses Yisrael: Malchus is reached through self-lowering, the inverse of the Calf that separated zeh from zos.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 256b — “The first commandment is called Anochi from the side of Keter, which is the Ayin of ‘our God.’ Anochi contains kaf—Keter—and contains ayin. Keter is called so from the side of the supernal Mother, in relation to whom the Torah mentions the departure from Egypt fifty times.” The source reads the letters of Anochi symbolically. The kaf, whose numerical value is twenty, supplies Rav Tzadok’s connection with the twenty gerah of a complete shekel.

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, Ki Sisa, opening discussion — “The Holy One, blessed be He, and Knesses Yisrael are called One; when Knesses Yisrael is in exile, that oneness is not manifest. Therefore the half shekel, ten gerah—the mystery of yud—must be drawn down to illuminate the place that was damaged. This is truly the ransom of his soul: through that half shekel judgment is removed. When good and the soul cleave together as one, it is called the sacred shekel, and silver, the King’s right side, is aroused toward the offering of Hashem.”

paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi Shekalim 2:3; Tanchuma, Ki Sisa 10 — “Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Nechemiah differed: One said, because they sinned at midday, they shall give half a shekel; the other said, because they sinned in the sixth hour, they shall give a half shekel equal to six small coins. Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Nechemiah said in Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s name: Because they transgressed the Ten Commandments, each shall give ten gerah. Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Levi’s name: Because they sold Rachel’s firstborn for twenty pieces of silver, and each received a coin, each shall give his shekel as a coin.” Tanchuma, Ki Sisa 10, also gives the midday, six-hour, Ten Commandments and sale-of-Yosef explanations. The Yerushalmi additionally relates the twenty silver pieces to redemption of a firstborn. These are distinct formulations, rather than a single undifferentiated statement.

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma, Ki Sisa 5; Vayikra Rabbah 8:1 — “Rabbi Yonah interpreted the verse concerning the expression zeh: With zeh they were brought low, and with zeh they were raised. With zeh they were brought low: ‘For this Moshe, the man.’ With zeh they were raised: ‘This they shall give.’ This is what Scripture says: ‘Righteousness raises a nation.’” Vayikra Rabbah 8:1 preserves the same contrast. Both passages also contrast Aharon’s involvement in “this calf” with “this is the offering of Aharon and his sons.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Devarim 12 — “What must be repaired then is that we merit the revelation of the hidden, the three upper levels, so that Keser Elyon is Keser Malchus, as it will be in the World to Come.” Rav Tzadok there places the same union in the repair sought in the three haftaros of punishment, showing that what the shekalim restore is a foretaste of the future revelation.

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, Ki Sisa, on the sale of Yosef — “Come and see: This ransom is fit to atone for the ten tribes who sold Yosef, separated zeh from zot, and transgressed their Master’s commandments. Therefore the shekel is twenty gerah, corresponding to the one who sojourned in a foreign land, was removed from the Holy Land, and was sold for twenty. From that hour Israel could not lift their heads because of that sin. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moshe: If you wish to lift their heads above, ‘This they shall give’—kol.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, Ki Sisa, on Kol and Knesses Yisrael — “Come and see: that Righteous One is called All, and the Congregation of Israel, the tenth of them all, is included in him. When they draw near to one another, they are called the holy shekel, because he is half a body and the Congregation of Israel is half a body. They join one another, and the body becomes complete. The twelve tribes beneath the sea draw nourishment, each one from its own place. This is what is written, ‘This they shall give’: ‘this’ has the numerical value twelve, corresponding to those who cling around the supernal Tabernacle.” The half shekel is explained here through mutual completion. Kol, “all,” is a title of the tzaddik, the channel of Yesod; the feminine side is Knesses Yisrael.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 176b — “The supernal holiness is known. The lower holiness is the wisdom of Shlomo; she too is summoned with all her hosts. All those hosts are ready to be crowned with this lower holiness when the appointed season rests upon the world. As her hosts stand above, so the appointed leaders of the people stand below after her pattern.” “The wisdom of Shlomo” is the source’s symbolic designation for the lower wisdom. Its contrast with supernal holiness supports Rav Tzadok’s distinction between the two aspects of the sacred shekel.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 297a — “Rabbi Elazar said: The beginning and ending of everything are included in holiness. Supernal Chochmah is called Holy, and when this supernal Chochmah shines, the wisdom of Shlomo shines, as it says, ‘Shlomo’s wisdom increased’—the moon stands in its fullness. When she is blessed from Yesod, we call her Holy, for he illuminates her completely. When she is not illuminated and crowned in fullness, we call her ‘the spirit of holiness,’ but she is not called Holy like the one above.” The source ties the lower wisdom’s title “Holy” specifically to receiving from Yesod. It therefore clarifies the role assigned here to Yosef, the tzaddik.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 166b — “The Holy One, blessed be He, sowed this light in His Garden of Eden, making it row upon row through that righteous one who is the garden's gardener. He takes this light, sows it as a seed of truth, and makes it row upon row in the garden; it gives birth, sprouts, and makes fruit, from which the world is nourished. This is 'Light is sown for the righteous.' ... These are the seeds of the first light, continually sown: now they give birth and make fruit, and now they are being sown. Before the world eats this fruit, that seed already gives birth and yields further fruit, without ceasing.” The gardener receives and plants the primordial light, rather than originating it. This is the precise connection with Yosef transmitting illumination to Malchus.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 86b — “The Rabbis taught: On the sixth of the month the Ten Commandments were given to Israel; Rabbi Yosei says, on its seventh. Rava said: All agree that they came to the wilderness of Sinai on Rosh Chodesh. ... And all agree that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbos. ... Their dispute concerns the fixing of the month.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 47b — “‘God completed on the seventh day’—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was completed, for it is the sustaining foundation of all. ‘His work which He had made,’ but not ‘all His work,’ for the Written Torah brought forth everything through the power of the writing that issues from wisdom. Three times ‘the seventh day’ is mentioned here: ‘God completed on the seventh day,’ ‘He ceased on the seventh day,’ and ‘God blessed the seventh day.’ ... This is the Oral Torah, for with this seventh day the world was completed.” The source expressly identifies the seventh day with the Oral Torah and places it beside the Written Torah’s emergence from Chochmah. This supports the twofold illumination with which the maamar concludes.
